To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have developed a method for learning generative latent representations of voxel models, which allows for the reconstruction of voxel models from partial and corrupted input data, and for the classification of voxels into object classes based on their latent representation, which we have demonstrated through the use of a simple application for 3D reconstruction from 2D images.
• Volumetric Auto-Encoders can be used to learn latent spaces for 3D objects, and that • The latent representations can be used to predict and classify 3D objects from sliding window segments.
we have shown that the use of variational auto-encoders for 3D object classification, prediction and denoising is feasible and can be extended with novel architectures.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the problem of unsupervised object classification and prediction in 3D through semantic sampling.
the problem of unsupervised learning and prediction of 3D object models from partial and noisy input.
the development of a new class of deep learning models for the unsupervised classification and prediction of 3D objects.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the proposed architectures can be used for classification and prediction of objects in a latent space, and that this is done through semantic sampling of 3D object segments, but that further research into the latent space is necessary for more accurate and robust predictions.

although voxel representations are visually interesting and intuitive to work with, their sparsity and high computational requirements are not conducive to learning structured high-level 2D and 3D filters.

although VAEs are not yet able to reconstruct 3D objects from sparse and semantically scaled input data, the proposed LVAE and PVAE architectures are able to learn a latent space that can be used for classification of 3D objects.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have shown that the variational reconstruction networks are able to learn complex latent spaces that are capable of representing and reconstructing complex 3D shapes and that these networks are also capable of learning complex generative latent spaces for denoising.
we are able to show the ability of VAEs to reconstruct and repair complex and varied noises.
we have demonstrated that it is possible to use variational auto-encoders for unsupervised learning of latent 3D spaces, which can then be used to reconstruct and classify 3D models.
The main takeaway from our work is that

although voxel models can be useful in the context of learning structured 3D filters for reconstruction, they cannot be used to train a generative model that can learn a high level representation of 3D objects.
although voxel representations are useful for 3D object visualization, the computational cost of learning from them is too high for practical use.
the latent space of the VAE is a good place for object representation.
